A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EasySpec, with matching algorithms and experiments. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original throughput, latency, acceptance-rate, hidden-state similarity, and ablation results in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports additional model configurations, an MLP-parallelization ablation, and vLLM scaling measurements.

M1.justification: Fuzzy attention-layer speculation, sequential MLP execution, tree attention, and bonus KV-cache calibration remain the same. The expanded strategy discussion and new ablations explain or test existing components rather than introduce a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MMLU, HumanEval, MATH, IFEval, MGSM, and the same six Spec-Bench task categories. Additional drafter sizes, target-model configurations, and inference-engine measurements do not introduce new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Vanilla decoding, TP, +SD, +tree, and EAGLE-2 remain the direct comparators. Vanilla results move to v2 Table 9 rather than disappear. vLLM is added to the TP-scaling diagnostic, without a direct comparison against EasySpec.

E3.justification: The Spec-Bench comparison changes temperature from 0 to 0.8 and EasySpec's drafter from 8B to 1B. v2 also evaluates five additional draft/base model pairings in Table 8 and introduces full-layer parallelization and vLLM evaluation configurations. These substantially extend experimental settings within retained tasks.

E4.justification: v2 Appendix B/Table 5 adds an ablation testing attention-only versus full-layer parallelization. Appendix D.1/Table 6 adds a vLLM replication of the TP-scaling analysis to examine implementation dependence. These provide substantive new checks of component selection and the system-level motivation; the original cosine-similarity and calibration/tree-width/LP-size analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report throughput variance across Spec-Bench items. v2 checklist item 7 newly states that repeated trials show negligible variation and explains omitting error bars and confidence intervals, but supplies no run counts or seeds. This is added disclosure, not evidence of an increased number of runs.

E6.justification: v2 replaces the Spec-Bench scores under changed settings: EasySpec's mixed throughput rankings against EAGLE-2 for Llama-3-70B become wins across all six tasks. Tables 5, 6, and 8 add ablation, engine, and model-pairing results. Most original benchmark values remain, but the temperature-0 Llama-3-70B(8B) HumanEval verification time changes from 1.57 to 1.63 seconds per 100 tokens.

T1.justification: Appendix E adds limited informal mathematical arguments connecting normalization and cosine similarity to approximation precision, plus an aggregate latency model involving drafting time and acceptance rate. Existing sampling mathematics and layer-execution equations are largely retained; no new formal theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains training-free, lossless speculative decoding through layer parallelism and bonus calibration. Both abstracts retain the headline 4.17x overall speedup, 1.62x drafting speedup, and at most 7% speculation-accuracy reduction. The explicit plug-in description does not materially redefine this contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for keeping MLPs sequential and excluding boundary layers, and reframes the drafter discussion around shallowness rather than simply parameter size. Appendix F newly qualifies acceleration as hardware- and implementation-dependent. The main accuracy-versus-latency interpretation remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and discloses chain-of-thought generation capped at 128 tokens, speculation length 5, and smaller-drafter LP settings. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously unspecified settings. Conversely, the explicit PyTorch-distributed implementation statement and v1's detailed alternative Llama-3-8B grouping rows are no longer supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and citations for SpecExec, OPT-Tree, PEARL, and SpecTr, plus a vLLM/PagedAttention citation for the additional measurements; the PyTorch reference is removed. The claimed novelty concerning multi-GPU utilization of existing drafters remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: layer-parallel strategies move into the method section, while TP-scaling, task-specific results, and tree-attention explanation move into appendices. Method explanations and the generalization discussion are expanded or rewritten, and dedicated theoretical-backing, limitations, and checklist sections are added.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the separate architecture/calibration illustrations with an expanded comparative overview, separates the GPU timeline, adds a cosine-similarity schematic, and redraws Figure 4. Tables are reorganized, including a condensed main results table with detailed values in Appendix Table 9. The document also changes from two-column to single-column layout.

improvement.justification: The new MLP ablation, smaller-drafter evaluations, and vLLM scaling check strengthen empirical support for the existing design, while clearer diagrams and newly disclosed decoding settings improve usability and reproducibility. The gain is limited: vLLM does not validate EasySpec end to end, and Appendix E.1 introduces a mathematically invalid general assertion that LayerNorm preserves cosine similarity.
